summary:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive website that tells the stories of eight machines NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars: Surveyor 3, the Apollo 11, 12 and 15 hardware, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity.

Each machine gets a first-person story, a plain-language account of what it did, where it rests today and what scientists learned from it. An interactive globe shows where each one sits, and 3D models let visitors inspect the hardware. An Explorer Passport tracks which machines a visitor has met, and a short quiz tests what they learned.

The project addresses the challenge by treating discarded equipment as a record of human exploration rather than as debris. It makes that history easy for students and the public to explore. It is a learning tool, not a game, and every fact links back to NASA sources.
details:
What it does. Visitors start on a landing page and choose the Moon or Mars. A 3D globe pins each machine’s resting place. Opening a machine shows its story, a first-person storyboard, mission dates, coordinates, experiments, achievements, what scientists learned, a fun fact and a photo gallery. The Explorer Passport records discoveries in the browser, and the quiz covers all eight machines. A References page lists every source.

Impact. It gives students and general audiences a short, readable route into NASA mission history. The tone is friendly, and text-to-speech narration supports different reading levels.

Tools. React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, three.js with react-three-fiber and drei, Framer Motion and Lucide icons. A small Flask server can serve the built site. The data lives in JSON files.

Creative choices. The “Zzz, resting” framing treats each machine as a character, not a relic. We chose an informative site over a game so the facts stay accurate and the content stays the focus.

Factors considered. Source accuracy, coordinates taken from NASA and LROC pages, performance (we replaced a 54 MB Moon model with a 1 MB texture), and mobile layout.
